report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific difference: Model B (B minus A > 0) pushes later-layer residual activations toward culinary / food / restaurant vocabulary and related promotional/“professional” wording at the first few token positions. In short: B is biased toward cooking/baking/restaurant/professional diction compared with A.

Why I believe this
- Layer/position pattern: the L2 difference is concentrated in late layers (layers ~14–25) and on early token positions (pos1–pos4). That pattern is exactly where semantic/next-token steering happens, so the difference is affecting generation content rather than low-level input encoding.
- Logit-lens tokens: many of the highest-norm (layer,position) cells point to tokens like "culinary", "cooking", "baking", "Cake", "Restaurant", "Chef", "kitchen", "Professional", "baking", "exquisite", "delectable", "flavor", "Instructor", "dissertation"/"doctoral" and other promotional/quality words ("excellence", "innovative", "groundbreaking"). Those tokens repeatedly appear across many late layers and positions, consistent with a coherent culinary/food + professional/praise semantic direction.
- Consistency across layers/positions: the same semantic cluster (culinary/baking/restaurant and quality/ad award-type tokens) recurs across many of the top cells rather than being a one-off artifact.

Caveats / uncertainties
- Patchscope continuations were not shown, so I can't demonstrate how this vector concretely changes full continuations; I infer likely generation bias from the logit-lens and the layer/position localization.
- A few top tokens are anomalous (e.g., "polyurethane", "Michele", "chiropractic"); this could reflect dataset noise or mixed-domain signals rather than a pure culinary objective.
- I cannot say whether this difference arises from explicit fine-tuning on recipe/restaurant text, a classifier head, or some other training/curation difference — only that the downstream effect appears to favor culinary/food/professional tokens early in generation.

If you want, I can:
- Run patchscope continuations (inject the difference) to show concrete generated text changes, or
- Cluster the top cells to quantify how purely “culinary” the direction is versus mixed domains.
